OperationalQueueRowV2.description: OperationalQueueItemV2 plus the OPTIONAL additive FE-042 incident_links; absent on a server that predates it. A current server always sends it (possibly with zero authorized links). The workflow detail keeps the unextended item.

OperationalStatusCountsV2.description: FE-043. Server-counted status distribution over the SAME repeatable-read snapshot, minted audit scope and applied filters as total_count, filtered_count and the page rows; not page rows and not separate status calls. Supported dimensions are exactly triage_state, verification_result, source_status and severity, each zero-filled over its closed domain. Each dimension counts the authorized set under every applied filter EXCEPT its own (own filter ignored so a selected KPI tile still shows its siblings); own_filter_applied says whether such a filter was dropped. Therefore: with no own filter, total equals filtered_count; with one, counts[selected value] (zero for a value outside the closed domain) equals filtered_count and total>=filtered_count; always total<=total_count and sum(counts)==total. Counts ignore cursor, limit and sort. 'SUCCEEDED' (source_status or verification_result) is the Portal queue record's state only (succeeded_means): it is NOT financial APPLIED, NOT projection convergence and NOT venue success; no source, projection or venue claim is made. environment, target_type, target_id and command_key are filters but not count dimensions. Runtime additionally enforces these arithmetic invariants.

OperationalIncidentLinksV2.description: FE-042. Per operation, at most 3 links, newest link first (link time descending, then incident id descending in byte order). BOTH ends must be authorized for the caller: the operation row is inside the minted audit scope AND the incident's own target/environment tuple is inside the SAME minted scope; operation access never implies incident access and no incident is picked as 'the' incident. Links to incidents outside the scope are omitted AND not counted, so an empty or short list never proves that no other incident exists; authorized_link_count counts only authorized links and truncated is true exactly when it exceeds items.length. Incident target types outside ACCOUNT/PORTFOLIO/DEPLOYMENT are never authorizable here. Read in the same repeatable-read snapshot as the page. Runtime additionally enforces items.length==min(authorized_link_count,3), truncated, and unique incident ids.

OperationalIncidentLinkV2.description: One current many-to-many link row (execution_incident_operation_links) to an incident whose OWN target tuple the caller is independently authorized for. LINKED publishes only incident id, relationship, link time and a minimal current-root summary (target, environment, severity, workflow_state); never title, prose, actors, evidence or counts. link_history is always the typed NOT_PUBLISHED / ORIGINAL_INCIDENT_TARGET_NOT_ATTESTED absence: the link is a current pointer and does NOT attest the incident's target when the link was written. NOT_ATTESTED keeps the slot and the count for an authorized link whose id or time cannot be represented exactly; it is never dropped.

ActivationPlanReadV2.description: Finite stored Portal metadata under current maintenance.read plus exact TS-qualified ROOT audit and reviewed Activation field seals. Explicit environment is a CURRENT technical perspective, not captured native origin; no role/read_all authority or source verdict. Historical plan expiry is not read expiry. Exact flags are validated, not masked. Missing capabilities NOT_RECORDED do not invent default versions. Evidence and compatibility are independently optional; private signatures/prose/actors/request/hash witnesses never disclose or enter public revision. SAME issuer-bound flight holds bodies AND contextual errors through fresh source and LAST Core/session/clock checks. No GET writes or activation. Runtime additionally verifies exact stored timestamp chronology and state/child/head integrity. Standard JSON Schema validates finite scalar/closed shape and cannot express sibling timestamp ordering; AJV shape validation alone is not that producer-integrity proof.

Different author with full exact current audit is allowed; explicit F0 routes retain their own-author ceiling. OperationalQueueV2.description: Counts are scoped BEFORE filters/page/sort/edge probes to current supported audit tuples. Nonzero authority with zero rows is EMPTY; no authority is404. No ADMIN/read_all/creator bypass or actor/prose/source journal disclosure. Optional additive amendment (FE-042/FE-043): rows may carry incident_links and page may carry status_counts, both read in the same repeatable-read snapshot; see OperationalIncidentLinksV2 and OperationalStatusCountsV2. TypedCondition.$comment: expires_at must be on or after deadline when both values are non-null; enforced by the application semantic validator

source_route_state.description: CURRENT_PRIMITIVE_CONFIRMED is emitted for exactly ops/emergency-close (N16B: the one source-as-is protective primitive accepted for compatibility). It is not an activation: portal_reachable stays false and runtime_active is false.

classification.description: Optional here only because the pinned extract fixture predates it (execution-command-catalog.valid.json is immutable evidence in the N16B acceptance record). ServedCommandCatalogue, the 200 body of the route, requires it on every entry. CONNECTED is not a member: every F0 entry has portal_reachable false, and the service refuses to emit a CONNECTED classification rather than publish a sendable claim under catalogue_revision 2.

capability_state.description: Constant under catalogue_revision 2. The service used to compute PARTIAL when any entry classified CONNECTED; that branch was unreachable (every entry is portal_reachable false) and contradicted this constant, so it was removed rather than published. A transport activation needs catalogue_revision 3, not a widened constant.

ServedCommandCatalogue.description: What GET /api/v1/execution/commands/catalog serves: CommandCatalogue where every entry carries `classification`. Canonical example: fixtures/execution-command-catalog.served.valid.json, generated by the same function the service applies to the same extract (apps/control-api/test/be-p13-catalogue.spec.ts compares them entry by entry).

payload.$comment: Application validator enforces HASH_ONLY_NO_RAW storage, max 32768 UTF-8 bytes, depth 6, 512 nodes, 128 array items, 4096-character strings, and forbidden sensitive key fragments

current_primitive.description: null for every command except ops/emergency-close (N16B), whose accepted-but-DARK current primitive is described here. runtime_active and source_side_effect_requested are constants false. The served plan always carried this key; it was missing from the schema (BE-P13).

CostImpactAbsence.description: FE-020. No plan or preview carries a cost, fee or impact estimate, so the only value is this typed absence. The client never computes one. A real estimate would need a source that publishes it and arrive as a new, versioned branch.

ExecutionCommandApplyRequest.description: F0 apply is DENIED-only: no body of this request can reach ACCEPTED, SUCCEEDED or a source request, so no success schema exists. request_key (BE-P13) makes the denial replayable and recoverable (same key + same operation => the same typed answer with replayed true; same key + another operation => REQUEST_KEY_PAYLOAD_CONFLICT). It is not a dedupe key for an effect: there is none.

F0ApplyDecision.description: details of the 409 COMMAND_RELAY_DISABLED body: the six RelayDenied fields (unchanged) plus the key and whether this answer is the stored one repeated. retry_allowed and source_request_sent are constants false: the denial happens before any relay or source call.

F0ApplyDeniedProblem.description: The only answer F0 apply gives once the plan is visible to its creator: 409 with this body. Exactly what the shared error filter sends (no public_copy_key/safe_next_action).

F0ApplyKeyConflictProblem.description: 409 when request_key was first used for a different operation of the same actor. Nothing is recorded and nothing is sent; the other operation is not named.

F0ApplyAttemptLookup.description: Read-only recovery of an F0 apply answer by request_key, for a client that lost the response. Keyed by the session actor; the named operation's exact target needs current TS-accepted audit.read BEFORE the attempt is read and again after. NONE: this actor never recorded that key in this workspace. FOUND: the key was recorded for THIS operation; relay_decision is what a replay returns. CONFLICT: the key is bound to a different operation of the same actor, which is deliberately not named.

read_truth.description: Truth for the exact server-bound queue request. EMPTY does not assert that a workspace has no operations outside the requested filters or opaque cursor.
